dataset_source.format: Zeek/Bro conn.log.labeled (tab-separated first 20 fields + 3-space separated tunnel_parents, label, detailed-label)

apafc_14_pipeline.reason: 6 of the 14 APAFC features (`mqtt_qos`, `mqtt_payload_bytes`, `coap_code`, `http_status`, `sixlowpan_dispatch`, `payload_entropy`) require application-layer headers or raw packet payloads that do not exist in Zeek `conn.log.labeled`. Furthermore, the existing `edge_ids.onnx` artifact was trained on synthetic 15-class IoT protocol profiles, whereas IoT-23 contains real Zeek connection summaries for Mirai/Okiru/Torii/HorizontalPortScan/DDoS/C&C traffic.

feature_breakdown.notes: APAFC maps L7 IoT protocols: mqtt=1, coap=2, http=3, sixlowpan=4, other=0. Zeek conn.log records L4 `proto` (tcp/udp/icmp) and L7 `service` (http, dns, ssh, irc, ssl, dhcp). HTTP flows are identifiable via service=='http' or port 80/8080; MQTT/CoAP/6LoWPAN must be inferred by port (1883/8883, 5683, 61616), else 0.
Zeek `duration` is in seconds (float). `duration_ms = float(duration) * 1000.0` (0.0 when unset `-`).
Bidirectional byte count = `orig_bytes + resp_bytes` (or `orig_ip_bytes + resp_ip_bytes` when L4 payload bytes are unset `-`).
Directly computed from bidirectional byte count and packet count.

Zeek conn.log does not store the raw TCP header flags byte integer, but records connection `history` letters (S=SYN, h=SYN+ACK, A=ACK, D=DATA/PSH, F=FIN, R=RST) and `conn_state` (S0, SF, REJ, RSTO), which map deterministically to a reconstructed TCP flags bitmask.

edge_iiotset_61_pipeline.reason: 56 of the 61 Edge-IIoTset features are deep packet inspection fields across MQTT (12), CoAP (9), HTTP (8), 6LoWPAN (9), DNS (6), Modbus/TCP (5), ARP (3), and ICMP/TCP flags that are not present in Zeek flow-level connection logs.

schema_compatibility.recommendation: 1. Keep the existing 14-feature `edge_ids.onnx` and 61-to-14 `lgbm_ids_bundle.joblib` models untouched for their respective schemas. 2. Provide an explicit `map_zeek_to_apafc14()` adapter (documenting that the 6 L7/payload features are zero-filled) to demonstrate why naive zero-shot transfer across incompatible feature modalities degrades accuracy. 3. Use a dedicated, leak-free 16-feature Zeek Connection Feature Extractor (`extract_zeek_native_features`) with capture-aware or chronological splitting for honest offline evaluation on IoT-23.
